title: Decent office machine, but limited for real power
body: The laptop itself is fine for basic tasks, but it's definitely not a high-end workstation. I bought this for AI development and system architecture work, and it's honestly underpowered in the graphics department. It has the Intel Core Ultra 7, but it relies on integrated Intel Arc graphics instead of a dedicated GPU. I actually had to spend time troubleshooting just to get the system to stop defaulting to the integrated graphics for tasks that it clearly couldn't handle. For a 16-inch "AI PC," you'd expect a designated high-end GPU, but this machine just doesn't have the muscle for Rendering or complex CAD work. It's "AI" in name, but limited in practice. The design is sleek and the Architecture of the build feels solid, with comfortable White keys that make for a good typing experience if you're just doing office work. But for anything involving Rendering or heavy data processing, it falls short. The real reason for the low score, though, is the Walmart/Allstate partnership. They promise to send your protection plan contract within 48 hours, but they didn't send mine for nearly a month—waiting until I was stuck and couldn't cancel it. Walmart dumps you onto Allstate, and Allstate uses the "sale price" on your receipt to lowball you if anything actually breaks. Good screen, decent build, but underpowered hardware and a scammy warranty partnership make it hard to recommend for anybody doing more than just checking emails. Don't waste your time. title: Great laptop! No regrets buying this one!
body: Purchased this item during Black Friday and the price was under $500 and well worth it! This was a gift for my wife. The screen is bright and the keyboard types very well. It doesn't miss a bunch of keystrokes like my work laptop. The track pad is butter smooth. The touchscreen works great too, even though we rarely use it. The processor is decent and with the RAM, it gets the job done. My wife uses it mostly for school, but as she is doing her Masters, she constantly has a ton of tabs and programs open at one time for research. I had her leave it unplugged to test the battery and although I can't remember how many hours of continued use it ran before needing a charge, it was quite a long time. It should be able to get you through the school day with battery to spare. So long as you aren't streaming movies the whole time. Even then, you may make it the entire day with battery left over. LOL We don't play games on it so I couldn't tell you how well they do or don't play. All in all, this was a great buy. I am cheap and would probably purchase this laptop even when not on sale now that I know how good it performs. Hopefully I will be able to start shooting videos for YouTube soon, so we will see how well it is able to edit the videos. I know it doesn't contain a separate GPU, but the embedded graphics processor should be able to handle the load... hopefully.
